A reverse auction is the opposite of a normal auction.

In a normal auction, buyers push the price up. In a reverse auction, sellers push the price down to win your order.

It runs for a fixed time, usually 15 to 60 minutes. Each supplier sees only where they stand (L1, L2, L3…), never the others' names. Anyone can lower their bid until the clock ends.

Large companies have bought this way for years. GetL1 makes it simple enough for any factory.

A common worry about reverse auctions is that they're unfair to suppliers.

In practice:
• Every supplier decides their own price. Nobody is forced to go below cost.
• Names and prices of other bidders are never shown.
• Late bids extend the clock, so nobody is sniped in the last second.
• The buyer can award to L2 or L3 for better delivery or quality, and records the reason.

A fair process is good for both sides. It's how long-term supplier relationships get built.
